warnings: Grid derived per project precedence rule from the structural footing/pedestal plan S-02 (หน้า25), which agrees exactly with the structural column/beam/floor plan S-03 (หน้า26) and with the architectural site plan A-03 (หน้า05) and floor plan A-04 (หน้า06) — 4 independent sheets agree, no conflict found.
x_lines dimension chain (S-02/A-04): 1-2 = 4.00 m, 2-3 = 4.00 m, 3-4 = 1.50 m (grid 4 sits at the building's east edge, matching the printed overall '9.50').

y_lines dimension chain (S-02): A-B = 4.00 m, B-C = 4.00 m, C-D = 2.00 m, D-E = 3.50 m; the printed overall bracket '13.50' on S-02 spans A to E (4.00+4.00+2.00+3.50=13.50), confirming this reading over an initial mis-read of A-03's site-boundary dimension chain (which includes non-grid site-setback distances '1.10'/'2.00'/'5.50' that are NOT part of the structural grid — the carport slab and site boundary extend beyond grid E, but grid E itself is fixed by the D-E=3.50 footing/column line on S-02/S-03).

No dummy grid lines were needed for this house: every footing (F5/F8/F10/F3), column (C1/C2/C0), and beam endpoint (B1-B6X, B3A, B3X, B4X, BX) sits exactly on a named grid intersection on S-02/S-03. The carport's light-steel structure (RB1/RB2 rafters, P1 post, SB1/SB1X/SB2 purlins on S-04/S-05) also lands on the same main grid (columns 1-4, rows A-D) — the purlin spacing dimensions (1.00/5.50/1.00 on S-04, and the roof-overhang dimensions on A-05/A-06/A-07) are secondary-member/overhang dimensions, not additional grid lines, since they carry no beam/column endpoint of their own per the beam-endpoint rule (§4).
Both dimension chains close against their printed overall dimensions: x = 9.50 m (4.00+4.00+1.50), y = 13.50 m (4.00+4.00+2.00+3.50).

One dummy x-grid was added: '1'' at pos_m=2.30, per the beam-endpoint rule (§4) — beam B2 on S-03 (แปลนเสา คาน และพื้น, หน้า26) sits on the partition wall between the two ห้องน้ำ (bathrooms), which the architectural floor plan A-04 (หน้า06) dimensions explicitly as 2.30 m + 1.70 m = 4.00 m within the grid-1-to-grid-2 bay — so its position (2.30 m from grid 1) is read from a printed dimension, not estimated. Named per the above/left rule: dummy grid takes the main grid to its left (grid '1') with a prime appended.

z_levels[] built 2026-08-28 by merging the element_type:"level" entries this house's own already-extracted sheets carry (schema section 4: one z_levels[] per building, merged across every sheet that prints levels). Transcription only -- no value was computed and no level was invented; each entry keeps the source_image of the sheet it was read from. Deduplicated on level_m, keeping the printed Thai label and recording any competing label from another sheet in confidence_flags. An installation-height schedule (fixture mounting heights) is deliberately NOT a source -- those are not building levels. dimension_chains[]/unassigned_dimensions[] are still un-swept for this house.

This house's grid master (op1 output) was already unusually clean before this sweep: every footing/column/beam endpoint sits on a named grid intersection, and only one dummy ('1\'' at x=2.30) existed pre-sweep, added under the older beam-endpoint rule (§4, before rule 4/2026-09-27) for beam B2's partition-wall landing point. No page read in this sweep prints an explicit '2.30/1.70' split on the x-axis to independently re-confirm '1\''s position from a fresh dimension row — it is left exactly as-is per op_fix's scope (only §4-rule-4 sweep additions are this staging file's job, not re-litigating pre-existing correct entries).

New dummy x-line @-1.5 (pos_m=-1.50, before grid 1): the roof/eave overhang measured consistently on the roof plan (หน้า07), all 4 elevations (หน้า08-11 via mirrored views), both sections (หน้า12-13), the carport structural plan (หน้า27) and the roof-structure plan (หน้า28), plus the top row of the two EE-series sheets (หน้า43-44, the one clean/matching row on those sheets). High confidence.

New dummy x-line @3.0 and @10.5 (carport roof width: grid2-1.00=@3.0, grid4+1.00=@10.5): read from the roof plan's carport eave bracket (1.00/5.50/1.00=7.50 total, หน้า07) and reconfirmed identically on the carport structural plan (หน้า27). High confidence — both ends resolve via two independent printed rows on the same sheet (1.00 segment and the grid2-grid4=5.50 middle segment, which itself checks out exactly against known grid2/grid4 positions).

New dummy y-line @-1.5 (pos_m=-1.50, before grid A) and @9.5 (pos_m=9.50, past grid C): the main hip roof's north/south eave overhangs, read from elevation 2 (หน้า09, mirrored on หน้า11) and reconfirmed on the carport plan (หน้า27, where the C-to-@9.5=1.50 tick marks the carport structure's own north edge) and the roof-structure plan (หน้า28). High confidence.

New dummy y-line @8.5 (pos_m=8.50, between C and D: C+0.50): a redundant/emphasis sub-bracket splitting the C-D=2.00 span into 0.50+1.50, printed identically on the floor plan (หน้า06), roof plan (หน้า07), beam/column plan (หน้า26) and the mechanical plan (หน้า45). High confidence — 4 independent sheets agree exactly.

New dummy z-level entries: datum ±0.00 'ระดับอ้างอิง' (never explicitly registered in z_levels[] before this sweep even though the existing 3 named levels are all relative to it), plus three unlabeled roof/canopy heights for the carport (0.20 floor, 3.00 soffit, 3.40 ridge) read as a clean printed z-chain on elevation 1 (หน้า08) and reconfirmed on elevations 2 and 4 (หน้า09, หน้า11) and section 2 (หน้า13). The 0.20 value also independently matches the 'จอดรถ +0.20' spot-level printed on the floor plan (หน้า06) and site plan (หน้า05) room labels. High confidence.

New dummy y-line @15.0 (carport structural frame's far/south edge, @9.5+5.50): read from a clean '5.50' bracket on the carport structural plan (หน้า27, page-cropped and reconfirmed with a dedicated close-up — the bracket's own two end-ticks are unambiguous). FLAGGED FOR HUMAN REVIEW: this point (y=15.0) sits 0.5 m further south than the roof's own south eave overhang line at y=14.5 (E+1.00, from หน้า07/09/11) — i.e. the carport's structural steel frame would extend slightly beyond its own roof sheeting's edge, which is physically unusual (normally the roof overhangs the frame, not the reverse). Not corrected here since 5.50 is unambiguously printed and both anchor points (@9.5 and the bracket ticks) are clean; a human should check whether this is a real minor design detail (e.g. gutter/downpipe clearance) or a drafting inconsistency between the architectural roof-plan sheets and this structural sheet.

A second, smaller printed dimension inside the same carport-frame area on หน้า27 (a '1.00' from the frame's own top edge down to an internal purlin-reference line, next to the 'แปเหล็กสำเร็จรูป @0.50 ม.' note) was judged to be an element-internal roof-framing detail (purlin/fastener layout), not a building-grid axis tick, per §4's own carve-out ('a dimension inside one element's own detail ... stays on the element'). Left off dimension_chains/unassigned_dimensions entirely rather than guessed either way — flagging the judgment call here per op_fix's standing order.

หน้า43 (EE-03, แปลนไฟฟ้าแสงสว่าง) and หน้า44 (EE-04, แปลนเต้ารับไฟฟ้า) both carry a second, OUTER dimension row/column (top: 3.00/8.00/1.60/1.50; left: 2.00/1.10/4.00/8.00/4.00/1.40/1.50/3.50/2.10, with grid rows printed E-D-C-B-A top-to-bottom — the only sheets in this set with that row order) that could not be confidently reconciled against the established grid within this sweep. The values are close to, but not exactly matching, known grid spacings in several places (e.g. 1.60 where 1.50 is expected, 1.40 where the known @8.5 split gives 0.50/1.50, 2.10/2.00 where no comparable site-plan value lines up cleanly), which reads as either a genuinely different reference boundary specific to these two electrical sheets, or accumulated small misprints/misreads. Per the instruction to flag rather than guess, every value from these two outer rows was placed in unassigned_dimensions with its source, and NO new dummy line was created from them. This is the single largest open item from this sweep and should be looked at directly on the original PDF/CAD source if available, since a page-image read could not settle it with confidence.
